takeaways: Private opinions, synchronized consensus, and centralized scalar scores are different institutions, not interchangeable reputation implementations.
Opinion synchronization can be necessary for indirect reciprocity, but public-heavy source mixing can also create polarization and fragmentation.
Centralized social-credit-style scores can reduce trust and cooperation and can keep stale judgments sticky against contradictory fresh behavior.
recommended_next_move: Publish reputation governance topology explicitly in the first richer reputation tranche.
Keep a mostly-private-opinion baseline before generalizing from synchronized or centralized reputation worlds.
If a centralized score is added, publish override and repair semantics and compare against a revisable local-reputation baseline.
